proposals.scope: Correct JPEG displayed/requested-time ownership only. The current archive end includes a one-second provisional tail and is not the decoded image's timestamp. Bind the JPEG image request/completion to the current camera, page session and request revision plus a proven media position/capture identity. Live pause must retain the actual owned still and its corresponding recorded clock, without a later metadata update moving that paused reading. Historical seeks/previews targeting an otherwise provisional future interval must clamp to proven recorded coverage or retain a valid owned selection rather than claim that unproven future timestamp for the old pixels. Local preview capture must label only the image that actually decoded for its owning position; it must not pair an old image with newer metadata or a pending seek's target. Preserve ordinary completed held-frame intervals and their progressing wall clock. Preserve the approved backend JPEG gap policy and bounded latest tail, unchanged legacy fields/URLs, session first-frame/opened_at/retention restrictions, bounded capture/request rate, one native video element/decoder, one committed gesture seek, recorded-only telemetry, Live, source/session reset and same-session replay recovery. Optional narrowly scoped internal JPEG frame descriptors and an optional selector on the existing JPEG frame endpoint are allowed only if needed to prove which capture a request will deliver; no new endpoint/provider, browser permission, public transport, capture loop, storage migration or product feature. Closed allowed-file list: optional files need not change. This is a closed allowed-file list, not a requirement to edit every optional file. A materially different API, new endpoint, CORS/header permission change, storage migration, provider capability change, extra file scope or capture/playback policy requires a revision before implementation. Prefer a descriptor on existing session metadata plus an immutable selector on the existing JPEG endpoint if needed. A legacy metadata response without that optional descriptor must remain compatible and must not invent proof of decoded-image identity. Keep all backend JPEG interval/gap/origin/first-frame arithmetic from P29/P31 unchanged except any narrowly necessary optional descriptor/selection access; do not collapse the gap or change the one-second internal provisional tail. A stable historical target inside a completed interval retains that target's existing wall clock, including while its image is held through a gap. Do not globally replace historical target time with capture-start time. Do not silently swap a paused still for a newer one merely to make it agree with an incorrectly saved future clock. Preserve the user's paused image intent using the owned position. No native HLS/continuous decoder construction, direct-browser/MJPEG policy, Cast capability, backend credential handling, printer control or storage namespace change.

proposals.risk: Moderate JPEG-only lifecycle/data ownership correction. The high-risk mistakes are timestamp-only association, label/clock publication before decode, stale completion after a source switch, incorrect treatment of completed held intervals, rounding across capture boundaries, and increasing request rate. The draft deliberately requires independent regression evidence for those cases before integration.

Corrected paused clock/position/rendered reading and cached preview must remain associated with blue. Verify normal one-second cadence and positive subsecond cadence, including non-half-second and non-millisecond capture positions. Do not pass the check by relying on rounded timestamps that select the preceding capture accidentally. Check explicit historical targets both inside a completed held interval and beyond the latest proven capture in the provisional tail; verify resulting archive-selected pixels, recorded time and thumbnail label agree. Hold a live image response, advance metadata, then finish the old image; reverse the order with a newer image/older metadata. Only proven owning request/completion may publish the displayed time or capture a thumbnail. Metadata alone is not an image identity. Hold an old JPEG completion across a committed seek, explicit Live, camera/session change, close and same-session reattachment. No stale callback may mutate the new source's display clock or preview history. Keep the same native video node and one page session across recovery. Test pause/play and explicit Live while a JPEG image is pending. Completed-history replay, the original thirty-second held-frame gap, later-page minimum/negative clock anchor and prior-page media exclusion must remain correct. During held pointer/key/wheel preview changes issue no intermediate main-image seeks; one release commits one target. Keep existing request/capture bounds and session-scoped deduplication. Verify optional descriptor/selector rejection and legacy-at compatibility without exposing prior-session footage or changing provider/origin boundaries. Standard no-recording live fallback must remain available without presenting an invented historical clock. Run focused affected units, the new bounded two-engine fixture and docs checks; a final core combined check belongs to integration. No real-device/LAN/external request or repeated stress run is needed.
